title: Cross-application references: per-hop ACL + redacted projection (reuse field-visibility) + hop-cap
commit_message: feat(T-0080): E11.9 cross-app references — per-hop ACL + redacted projection (reuse field-visibility) + hop-cap
design_note: Implements §6 'references, not copies' for cross-application data traversal. A cross_app_ref definition stores only the ref_field pointer (source registry → target registry via a JSONB UUID key); target record fields are never copied. Per-hop ACL re-check goes through an injected CrossAppHopFetcher port (which wraps the single PDP / resolveFor). Redaction reuses T-0081 FieldProjection (physical key absence, not null). Traversal is bounded by HOP_CAP = 3. Cross-process data stays within the RLS channel (the migration RLS predicate is the single tenant_id predicate, NF-1). Fail-fast on first denied hop prevents information leakage about chain structure beyond the denial point.

files_changed.description: Tenant-scoped DDL for choros.cross_app_ref: PK (tenant_id, id), FK to registry_def (source + target), ref_field text, label, ref_strength CHECK (weak/strong), RLS predicate (single tenant_id predicate NF-1), FORCE RLS, GRANT to choros_app, index on (tenant_id, source_registry_id).

Pure-core mechanism. Exports: CrossAppRefDef, CrossAppHopFetcher, CrossAppRefDeps, CrossAppHopResult, CrossAppHopDenied, CrossAppHopAllowed, HOP_CAP (=3), resolveHop(), resolveHopChain(), buildRedactedHopProjection(). No DB/IO/env. Imports only FieldProjection from field-visibility.ts (T-0081 brick reuse). Per-hop ACL via injected fetcher port (single PDP path). Hop-cap enforced in resolveHop step 1.

25 pure unit tests covering CR-1 through CR-16 + SECURITY test. Tests: per-hop deny (no_grant, not_found, cross_tenant), hop-cap at boundary (depth=HOP_CAP-1 allowed, depth=HOP_CAP denied), dangling refs (missing/null/non-string), allowed pass-through, redacted projection structural distinctness (no `value` key), chain traversal (all-allowed/fail-fast/second-denied), depth accumulation, empty chain.

Fitness check with --self-test. CA1: core purity (no pg/fs/net/http/crypto/process.env). CA2: no direct grant-resolver import (single authority path). CA3: FieldProjection imported from field-visibility (no fork). CA4: HOP_CAP exported and used in depth guard. CA5: resolveHop exported. CA6: no parallel ACL store tokens.

redaction_reuse_of_field_visibility.summary: cross-app-ref.ts imports FieldProjection from ./field-visibility.js (T-0081). The denied-hop sentinel shape is exactly FieldProjection & { visible: false } = { key, visible: false, redacted: true, label }. This is structurally identical to T-0081's Decision 4 (F-3): no `value` key, label/id only. buildRedactedHopProjection() returns this type. The CrossAppHopDenied interface wraps it as `redactedProjection: FieldProjection & { visible: false }`. No fork of the redaction sentinel — the same type is reused as pinned in T-0081 ADR §6.3 (Decision 6).
redaction_reuse_of_field_visibility.FieldProjection_used_as: CrossAppHopDenied.redactedProjection and the return type of buildRedactedHopProjection()

security_argument.no_second_authority_path: cross-app-ref.ts imports ONLY FieldProjection from field-visibility.ts and uses no grant algebra. All ACL decisions go through the injected CrossAppHopFetcher port, which is implemented in the adapter layer using resolveFor (the single PDP). Verified by CA2 static check.
security_argument.no_value_leak: Denied hops return { visible: false, redacted: true, label } — no value key. Allowed hops return fields already projected by the single PDP (T-0081 redaction already applied inside resolveFor). This module does not re-project or re-redact — it passes through the PDP output as-is. Verified by CR-8 test.
security_argument.hop_cap: HOP_CAP = 3 enforced in step 1 of resolveHop before any fetcher call. depth + 1 > HOP_CAP → denied(hop_cap_exceeded). Fetcher not called (verified by CR-3 test asserting mockFetcher not called).
security_argument.fail_fast_chain: resolveHopChain stops on first denied hop, preventing information leakage about chain structure beyond the denial boundary. Verified by CR-10 test asserting fetcher called exactly once.
security_argument.rls_channel: migration 068 has a single tenant_id predicate (NF-1, FORCE RLS, choros_app DML GRANT). Cross-process data exposure is within the RLS boundary. The pure core never bypasses RLS — all DB access is through the adapter layer.
